label: Kathleen H. Hicks
narrative: Every structural decision about the official UAP apparatus between 2021 and 2024 carries Hicks's signature. As Deputy Secretary of Defense she directed the establishment of the Airborne Object Identification and Management Synchronization Group on 23 November 2021, an entity built to answer Congress's Section 1683 mandate without disturbing anything below it. When AOIMSG proved inadequate she signed the memorandum of 15 July 2022 - announced 20 July - establishing the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office, disestablishing AOIMSG, ordering the Navy to shut down the UAP Task Force and hand its data and materials to AARO, and placing AARO under the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security. In late July and August 2023, with Grusch's testimony fresh, she pulled AARO out of the USD(I&S) chain and made its director report directly to her, saying the Department takes UAP seriously because they are a potential national security threat and a safety risk. That re-wiring is the most consequential organisational fact in the domain: it put the office that adjudicates whistleblower claims about concealed special access programmes directly under the deputy head of the department those programmes would be concealed within. Notably, Hicks did not publicly endorse the central findings of the Historical Record Report Volume I when it was released in March 2024, a silence Christopher Mellon flagged at the time - the report's assertions were made at the AARO level, never ratified at cabinet level.
